To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a significant fraction of protein-protein interactions reported in the current literature, and in genome-wide datasets of protein interactions, are inconsistent with known macromolecular structures, (2) individual interaction datasets are inherently noisy, and (3) simple Bayesian approaches can be used to combine them, significantly improving accuracy.
the current protein interaction networks contain many errors that are not obvious from their structure, but are easily detected by comparison to known complexes.

(1) many protein interactions reported in the scientific literature, in genome-wide studies, and in individual interaction datasets are incorrect, (2) genome-wide datasets, although noisy, are useful for generating hypotheses that are best tested using other methods, (3) the best way to use interaction datasets is to integrate them, and (4) Bayesian methods are a good way to do this.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the integration of structural and genomic data, and with the validation and improvement of interaction datasets.
the reliability and coverage of the interaction networks that are being generated by high-throughput methods.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, while the genome-wide approaches are useful and informative for the identification of novel protein-protein interactions, their reliability needs to be carefully considered, especially when they are used to identify specific individual interactions.
the current state of protein interaction data is not sufficient for reliable genome-wide analyses.

(i) the majority of interactions reported in genome-wide datasets and the literature are incorrect, and this is a serious problem for their use; (ii) the best use of individual interaction datasets is in a Bayesian framework, where multiple datasets are integrated; and (iii) the most reliable interactions are those that are supported by more than one method and/or by multiple lines of evidence.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the reliability and coverage of genome-wide protein interaction datasets must be assessed by comparison to known structures and complexes, and the results of different methods integrated to improve the quality of the data.
, although genome-wide interaction datasets are valuable and useful for many purposes, their reliability must be carefully considered when interpreting individual protein interactions.
the reliability of protein interaction data can be assessed by comparison to the structures of known complexes, which can be used to guide and improve the design of future experiments.
